title: Trace an order event across failure boundaries
description: Switch scenarios to see which path survives a commit, redelivery, or incompatible consumer. Select any component to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Checkout API
nodes.detail: Accepts CreateOrder, validates the immediate request, and returns the committed order identity. It does not wait for every downstream reaction.

nodes.label: Order service
nodes.detail: Owns the order invariant. It commits the order and the publication intent in one local transaction before acknowledging success.

nodes.label: Order store
nodes.detail: Stores authoritative order state. Downstream projections may lag, but they cannot redefine whether the order was accepted.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.detail: Stores the event envelope in the same database transaction as the order. A relay can retry publication without guessing whether the business commit happened.

nodes.label: Event broker
nodes.detail: Retains or routes OrderCreated for independent subscriber groups. Its acknowledgement and redelivery rules are part of the application contract.

nodes.label: Inventory projection
nodes.detail: Applies compatible order events in aggregate order. It rejects or quarantines a schema it cannot interpret instead of silently corrupting stock state.

nodes.label: Payment consumer
nodes.detail: Records the event ID with the charge in one local transaction. A duplicate delivery therefore converges on one business effect.

nodes.label: Recovery queue
nodes.detail: Preserves the event identity, schema version, error, attempt count, and correlation context for repair and controlled replay.

scenarios.label: Healthy outbox
scenarios.summary: CreateOrder commits authoritative state and an OrderCreated envelope together. The relay publishes later, and each subscriber group advances independently.
scenarios.result: Checkout can return after the local commit. Inventory and payment may lag, but the durable outbox preserves a path from every accepted order to its event.

scenarios.label: Direct publish gap
scenarios.summary: The order transaction commits, then the service crashes before its separate broker publish completes. The database and broker now disagree about what happened.
scenarios.result: The customer has an accepted order, but no subscriber can discover it from the broker. A transactional outbox or database change stream closes this dual-write gap.

scenarios.label: Lost consumer ack
scenarios.summary: Payment commits a charge, but its acknowledgement is lost. The broker delivers the same event ID again because it cannot prove the first attempt completed.
scenarios.result: At-least-once delivery is safe only when the consumer records the event ID with the business effect. The retry then becomes a no-op instead of a second charge.

scenarios.label: Schema break
scenarios.summary: A producer replaces a required field without a compatibility window. Payment ignores that field, but the older inventory consumer cannot interpret the new event.
scenarios.result: One incompatible consumer fails without blocking the other group. Quarantine the event, restore a compatible contract, then replay from the preserved event identity and position.
